# 149. Autogenerated ids via an injected IDGen port

Status: Accepted — 2026-07-27. Spec:
[docs/specs/2026-07-27-processinstance-audit-view-and-idgen.md](../specs/2026-07-27-processinstance-audit-view-and-idgen.md).
Part of the ADR-0144…0149 delivery. Relates to the id generator seam in
[ADR-0138] (clock) and `runtime/idgen`.

## Context

Token, task, command, timer, incident, and scope ids are minted in the **pure
engine core** as `<InstanceID>-<prefix><seq>` — tokens `-t` (`step_state.go:49/60`),
tasks `-h` (`:129`), commands `-c` (`:124`), timers `-tm` (`:134`), incidents
`-inc` (`:141`), scopes `-s` (`state_compensation.go:221`), driven by per-instance
sequence counters. Consumers want ids that don't embed the instance id. The
project already ships `runtime/idgen` (`xid` default, `Generator` interface).

Two hard constraints on the core (`engine/purity_test.go`): it must **not** import
denied packages or read the wall clock (`time.Now`-family AST calls are rejected),
and it is **deterministic for replay**. `xid` is timestamp-based (reads the wall
clock) — so it **cannot** be called directly in the core. The id format is
**generated, never parsed** anywhere in prod, so changing it breaks no structural
dependency (only ~18 full-stack test files assert the literal format).

## Decision

Add an **`IDGen` seam** to `StepOptions`, defined **locally in `engine`**
(`type IDGen func() (string, error)` or a one-method interface) — **not** an alias
of `runtime/idgen.Generator`, which would create a `core → runtime` layering
inversion that compiles and passes `purity_test.go` yet violates the core-purity
principle. `runtime` adapts `idgen.Generator` to the local seam. Add `/runtime/` to
`engine/purity_test.go` `deniedEngineImports` to enforce the boundary. The pure
core **calls** the seam when minting each id; it never imports `xid` or reads the
clock, so `purity_test.go` still passes.

1. **Default = deterministic counter.** When `IDGen` is nil, the core uses the
   existing `<InstanceID>-<prefix><seq>` scheme — behaviour byte-identical to
   today. Engine-core tests and replay stay deterministic.
2. **Product boundary wires `xid`.** The service/runtime construction sets the
   default `IDGen` to `idgen.XID()`, so real instances get opaque, k-sortable,
   autogenerated ids across all six id kinds.
3. All **seven generation sites / six id kinds** route through the seam — tokens
   are minted at **two** sites (`step_state.go:49` and `:60`), plus command, task,
   timer, incident, scope. The full-stack tests that assert the `-tN`/`-hN` format
   are updated (or switched to the deterministic default); pure-engine tests using
   the default counter are unaffected.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** production ids are opaque and don't leak the instance id, while the
  core keeps its purity and deterministic-replay guarantees (the seam is the only
  new surface, and the default preserves current behaviour exactly).
- **Positive:** reuses the existing `runtime/idgen` abstraction — no new vendor
  coupling in the core.
- **Negative:** an injected non-deterministic generator makes a *product* instance
  non-replay-identical by id; this is acceptable because ids live in the persisted
  snapshot (not regenerated on load), and deterministic replay is preserved for the
  core/tests via the default. Documented as an explicit trade-off.
- **Negative:** ~18 full-stack tests churn; each id site needs a focused test that
  the seam is honoured and the nil-default is unchanged.
- **Risk:** a generator returning an error (rare, e.g. UUID entropy) must surface
  as a clean step error, not a panic — the `IDGen` signature returns `error` and
  each call site propagates it.

## Implementation amendments (2026-07-27, Phase 4)

- **The seam is named `engine.IDGenerator`** (field `StepOptions.IDGenerator`) —
  spelled out rather than abbreviated, matching `runtime/idgen.Generator`, which
  satisfies it STRUCTURALLY. No adapter, and no `runtime` import in the core;
  `/runtime/` is now in `engine/purity_test.go`'s `deniedEngineImports` to keep it
  that way.
- **Error propagation without threading errors through 40 call sites.** The mint
  sites (`placeToken`, `nextCommandID`, `openScope`, …) sit in helpers that cannot
  return an error. `Step` installs a transient, unexported `idSource{gen, err}` on
  the working clone; `nextID` records the FIRST generator failure there and returns
  a blank id; `Step` converts a recorded failure into the step's error and scrubs
  the seam from the returned state. A failed generation therefore never yields a
  usable state — the partially-built clone is discarded. `Step`'s trigger switch
  moved into an unexported `dispatch` so this wrapping lives in one place.
- **Counters still advance** under an injected generator: `TokenSeq`/`TaskSeq`/…
  are durable bookkeeping ("how many were minted"), independent of who names them.
- **Call-activity child ids** are still derived from the call command's id
  (`<parent>-sub-<commandID suffix>`), which is what makes a re-driven command
  idempotent. With xid that suffix is a constant ~20 chars, so id length still
  grows linearly with nesting depth — just with a larger constant. Tests that
  hard-coded the `-sub-c1` form now resolve child ids through the call-link store.
  ⚠ **Amended — see Implementation amendment 1 below. The "larger constant" was
  understated and the derivation was outright broken for opaque ids.**

## Implementation amendments (2026-07-28, code review)

### 1. Child-instance-id derivation had to be made generator-agnostic

The Consequences note above assumed the suffix extraction would keep working once
an `IDGenerator` was injected. It did not. The derivation was:

```go
// cmd.CommandID format is "<instanceID>-c<N>"   <-- no longer true
suffix := cmd.CommandID
if idx := strings.LastIndex(cmd.CommandID, "-"); idx >= 0 {
    suffix = cmd.CommandID[idx+1:]
}
childInstanceID := st.InstanceID + "-sub-" + suffix
```

An xid contains **no hyphen**, so `strings.LastIndex` returns −1 and `suffix`
becomes the *entire* 20-char command id. Each nesting level therefore appended
~25 characters rather than the ~8 the scheme was designed around. `maxCallDepth`
is 64, but MySQL's `instance_id VARCHAR(255)` overflows around depth 10 — so a
legal nesting well inside the guard failed with an opaque driver "Data too long"
error instead of the intended `ErrCallDepthExceeded`. The in-code comment
asserting the id format was false as of this ADR.

**Amendment:** the derivation is now `childInstanceIDFor(parent, commandID)`:

- If `commandID` is exactly `<parent>-c<digits>` — the engine's built-in counter
  form — the bare counter is used, so pre-ADR-0149 ids stay **byte-identical**.
- Otherwise (any generator-minted opaque id) the command id folds to a
  fixed-length digest, making per-level growth a constant 13 characters.
- A total-length cap folds an over-long derivation to a fixed short form, so a
  runaway chain trips `maxCallDepth` rather than the column width.

Determinism is preserved in every branch, which is what keeps a re-driven call
command idempotent — the property this ADR's original note was protecting.

### Test-suite consequence, measured (not estimated)

Wiring xid into the driver broke **14 tests in 2 packages** — every one of them
predicting an engine-minted id (`instanceID+"-tm1"`, `parentID+"-sub-c1"`,
`"rh-1-tm1"`). One of them, `TestTimerTxFlowArmCancelInterleave`, gated a fake
scheduler on a predicted timer id and therefore **hung until the 10-minute test
timeout** rather than failing fast.

That is the ADR's own "id format is generated, never parsed" rule being violated
by the tests. The fix was to resolve ids through the API that owns them rather
than to reconstruct them:

| Needed | Resolved from |
|---|---|
| a timer id | `TimerStore.ListArmed()` / the gated job's own `ID()` |
| a child instance id | `CallLinkStore.ChildrenOf(parent)` (or the pending notify) |
| a child with call-links disabled | `InstanceStore.List` minus the parent |

Tests that assert on an id SHAPE (`TestDriverEngineIDsDefaultToXID`) are the
deliberate exception: they exist to pin the strategy itself.
